acip: GNYIS PA MCHOD PA 'BUL BA NI PHYAG BYA BA'I YAN LAG ZIN PA DE (NAS MCHOD PA'I YAN LAG NI, MCHOD PA'I 'KHOR GSUM) STE MCHOD PA DANG, MCHOD YUL DANG, MCHOD MKHAN GSUM (PO RNAM PAR MI RTOG PA BDE STONG DBYER MED) KYIS (RGYAS BTAB NAS 'BUL BA) YIN LA, BDE STONG GI DON RGYAS PAR NI BLA MA'I MAN NGAG LAS BTZAL DGOS SO,,
wylie: gnyis pa mchod pa 'bul ba ni phyag bya ba'i yan lag zin pa de (nas mchod pa'i yan lag ni, mchod pa'i 'khor gsum) ste mchod pa dang, mchod yul dang, mchod mkhan gsum (po rnam par mi rtog pa bde stong dbyer med) kyis (rgyas btab nas 'bul ba) yin la, bde stong gi don rgyas par ni bla ma'i man ngag las btsal dgos so
english: This brings us to our second point, the presentation of offerings.  Now that the step of bowing is completed, the next step is to present Them with offerings.  We make our presentation then as follows, being sure to stamp the practice with our realization that the three elements of the act of giving--the gift, the one receiving the gift, and the giver--are indivisible bliss and voidness, beyond all conception.  Those of you who would like to understand this idea of bliss and voidness in greater detail should seek private instructions from your Lama on the matter.
